tests.name: Single server's tool count vs the model's cap
tests.what: Checks whether THIS ONE server's tool count alone would exceed the model's per-request cap. This is a single-server upper-bound check; the binding limit across all connected servers is ENV_AGGREGATE_TOOL_COUNT.
tests.rec: Split the server, disable unused tools, or enable tool-search/deferred loading so fewer than the cap are presented at once. On Gemini the 512 functionDeclarations cap is the wall; on OpenAI/Grok/Mistral trim to the 128/200 limit.

anthropic.rat: Anthropic has no fixed per-request tool-count cap, so a single server cannot be rejected on count here; the binding limits are AGGREGATE (see ENV_AGGREGATE_TOOL_COUNT) and the ~40 selection cliff (SERVER_TOOL_COUNT_PRACTICAL).
anthropic.cons: No fixed per-request count cap, so one server cannot be rejected on count here; the binding ceilings are the aggregate catalog max and the ~40 selection cliff.

tests.name: Tool-definition footprint vs context window
tests.what: The headline footprint test: what share of the model's context window the server's tool definitions consume before any user message. High shares starve the conversation. Single-server view; the window is shared across servers, so the binding share is ENV_AGGREGATE_FOOTPRINT.
tests.rec: Trim tool definitions or pick a larger-window model. The same server is trivial on a 1M-window model and crippling on Phi-4 (16K). Enable prompt caching so the static footprint is paid once.

anthropic.rat: Anthropic's 1,000,000-token window absorbs typical footprints; impact is mostly per-call cost, but a very high share (>=50%) still warns/fails via the verdict bands.
anthropic.cons: On a large window the footprint is a minor cost concern, not a fit problem.

tests.name: Total tools across all servers within the model's cap
tests.what: Sums the tools of ALL connected MCP servers (plus built-in/model tools) and checks the total against the model/host AGGREGATE cap — the limit that actually binds (Claude 10k catalog, OpenAI 128, Gemini 512, Cursor 40). This is the real tool-count gate; SERVER_TOOL_COUNT_HARD is only a single-server upper bound.
tests.rec: Trim the active server set, disable unused tools, or enable tool-search/deferral so the COMBINED tool count across all connected servers stays under the cap. The cap is an environment-wide budget shared by every server.

tests.name: Schema avoids unsupported keywords
tests.what: Detects JSON Schema keywords the target model does not support in tool schemas (OpenAI strict: oneOf/$ref disallowed; allOf limited), which cause rejection or silent mishandling.
tests.rec: Rewrite unions as nullable fields or split into separate tools; inline $ref shapes. For OpenAI strict mode, set additionalProperties:false and mark all properties required.

anthropic.rat: Anthropic is permissive about schema keywords, so this is low-impact here — but the same schema may fail on OpenAI.
anthropic.cons: Anthropic accepts a broad JSON-Schema subset; unsupported-keyword risk is mainly portability to stricter models.
anthropic.ev_val: Input JSON Schema for tools: supported schema keywords include type, properties, required, description, enum, anyOf, items, and most standard JSON Schema draft-07 keywords. The 'pattern' keyword is explicitly NOT supported when strict:true is used (returns 400 error). No documented maximum nesting depth, maximum properties count, or maximum total schema size. MCP toolset tools count identically to client tools as input tokens. Prompt caching can be applied to the tools parameter via cache_control on an mcp_toolset or individual tool definitions to cache repeated tool schemas at 0.1x input price after a cache write. The input_examples field (optional) adds ~20-200 tokens per tool. Strict mode (strict:true) enables schema-conformant tool calls and composes with defer_loading without grammar recompilation.

anthropic.rat: Anthropic is permissive about schema keywords, so this is low-impact here — but the same schema may fail on OpenAI.
anthropic.cons: Anthropic accepts a broad JSON-Schema subset; unsupported-keyword risk is mainly portability to stricter models.
anthropic.ev_val: Same as Opus 4.8. No documented maximum depth or total schema size for client tools. JSON Schema input_schema supported. 'pattern' keyword unsupported with strict:true. Prompt caching applicable to tool definitions.

anthropic.rat: Anthropic is permissive about schema keywords, so this is low-impact here — but the same schema may fail on OpenAI.
anthropic.cons: Anthropic accepts a broad JSON-Schema subset; unsupported-keyword risk is mainly portability to stricter models.
anthropic.ev_val: Same Anthropic tool schema shape. 200k window means tool definitions are proportionally more expensive as a % of window than on Opus/Sonnet. Strong case for using defer_loading to preserve context for actual work. 'pattern' keyword unsupported with strict:true.

openai.rat: OpenAI strict function schemas reject unsupported keywords (oneOf/$ref); the call fails until the schema is rewritten.
openai.cons: OpenAI strict mode rejects oneOf/$ref and requires additionalProperties:false with all-required.
openai.ev_val: JSON Schema for parameters follows OpenAI's structured outputs subset. Strict mode (strict:true) enforces: (1) additionalProperties must be false on all objects; (2) all properties must be listed in 'required'; (3) max 100 object properties total; (4) max 5 nesting levels; (5) anyOf supported only for nullable types (anyOf: [{type: X}, {type: null}]); (6) $ref not supported in strict mode; (7) oneOf/allOf have problems in strict mode; (8) keywords pattern, minLength, minimum, format are accepted but NOT enforced by the model. Non-strict mode accepts a broader subset. No documented byte-size limit on total tool definition payload beyond the context window.

Keywords pattern/minLength/minimum/format not enforced by model.

google-gemini.rat: Gemini supports more keywords than OpenAI strict but still rejects oversized/forced-mode schemas — usually fixable, occasionally blocking.
google-gemini.cons: Gemini 2.5+/3 added anyOf/$ref support, but very large/nested or ANY-mode schemas are still rejected.
google-gemini.ev_val: OpenAPI subset only for function parameters. Supported keywords (as of 2025-11 update for Gemini 2.5+ and Gemini 3 models): type, nullable, required, format, description, properties, items, enum, anyOf, $ref, minItems, maxItems, minimum, maximum. NOT supported in older models (pre-2.5): anyOf, oneOf, $ref, default, optional. For ANY function-calling mode the API may reject very large or deeply nested schemas — official docs recommend simplifying by shortening property names, reducing nesting, or limiting function declarations if errors occur. No documented maximum nesting depth or property count in official docs. Source: https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/function-calling (Notes and limitations section), https://ai.google.dev/api/caching#FunctionDeclaration

Supported keywords for Gemini 2.5 Pro (as a 2.5-series model with Nov 2025 schema update): type, nullable, required, format, description, properties, items, enum, anyOf, $ref, minItems, maxItems, minimum, maximum. Key additions vs older models: anyOf and $ref now supported (Gemini 2.5+, confirmed via Google structured-output announcement Nov 2025). ANY mode may reject very large or deeply nested schemas. No documented hard nesting depth or property count. Pricing has a long-context tier >200K tokens (higher rate) which may affect tool-heavy sessions. Source: https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/function-calling, https://ai.google.dev/api/caching#FunctionDeclaration
